articles.title: Matthew Moss Food Club Celebrates 10th Anniversary of The Bread and Butter Thing
articles.excerpt: The Matthew Moss Food Club marked the 10th anniversary of The Bread and Butter Thing, celebrating its role in supporting local families with affordable food options.
articles.content_html:
Members and volunteers at the Matthew Moss Food Club gathered to celebrate the 10th anniversary of The Bread and Butter Thing. The event highlighted the charity's significant impact, as the Rochdale club is one of over 160 hubs across England that provide essential food support to local communities.

The club offers three bags of food, including fresh fruit and vegetables, chilled items, and cupboard staples, all for a cost of £8.50. This initiative not only provides affordable food options but also fosters community connections, allowing members to meet neighbours and volunteer at the weekly hub.

Vic Harper, chief executive of The Bread and Butter Thing, expressed gratitude for the support from members, volunteers, and partners, stating, "People knowing they can rely on us, week after week, is only possible because of the dedicated members, volunteers and partners who make hubs like Matthew Moss such an important part of their community."

The Bread and Butter Thing began its journey with a hired van delivering surplus food to a community centre in Moss Side, Manchester, and has since grown to support over 100,000 households across more than 160 communities. The anniversary celebration serves as a reminder of the charity's ongoing commitment to alleviating food insecurity in the region.
